dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: Friend's Godaddy store UI is buggy and cumbersome for managing SKUs, prices, and variants; CSV is the known bridge format

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Variants and SKU rules handled cleanly, AI-assisted product descriptions, save time and reduce errors — all explicitly stated

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Import file parses correctly and products appear correctly on Godaddy; idempotent uploads confirmed; AI rewrite tested per-product

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: Explicitly defined: no payment/checkout, no order/inventory sync, no Godaddy API integration (CSV-only)

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: No contradictions found across all interview decisions and artifacts

problem: The user's friend manages a Godaddy ecommerce store selling branded merchandise (t-shirts, hats, mugs) across 3 product families.
Godaddy's store management UI is primitive and buggy for handling SKUs, pricing, variants, and product descriptions — making even basic operations tedious and error-prone.
The CSV export/import is the only reliable bridge, but Godaddy's CSV format is cumbersome: auto-generated SKUs are cryptic, variant relationships are implicit, and image handling is opaque.
goals: Handle variants and SKU rules cleanly — auto-generate readable, consistent SKUs from variant attributes instead of Godaddy's cryptic format
AI-assisted product descriptions — per-product rewrite button for generating or improving product copy
Save time and reduce errors — local web app for comfortable editing, validated CSV export for import

successCriteria.criterion: Import CSV parses correctly and products appear correctly on Godaddy after import
successCriteria.check: npx tsx src/index.ts export --input products.json --output test-export.csv && diff test-export.csv godaddy-products-export.csv (structural comparison — column order, variant relationships, SKU format)

successCriteria.criterion: Idempotent uploads — re-running export doesn't create duplicates or corrupt data
successCriteria.check: npx tsx src/index.ts export --input products.json --output export-1.csv && npx tsx src/index.ts export --input products.json --output export-2.csv && diff export-1.csv export-2.csv (should produce identical files)

successCriteria.criterion: SKU auto-generation produces consistent, readable SKUs from variant attributes
successCriteria.check: npx tsx src/index.ts export --input products.json --output test-export.csv && grep -c 'SKU' test-export.csv | assert > 0 && grep SKU test-export.csv | awk -F, '{print $1}' | sort -u | assert count matches expected unique SKU count

successCriteria.criterion: Images are organized into the correct directory structure for Godaddy import
successCriteria.check: npx tsx src/index.ts export --input products.json --output test-export.csv && find ./godaddy-images/ -type f | assert count matches number of unique product images

successCriteria.criterion: AI rewrite produces a usable product description for review
successCriteria.check: Judgment call — human verifies rewritten description is readable, appropriate, and better than the original

mvp.reason: Foundation for everything — without parsing the source format, nothing else works

mvp.reason: Core interaction model — replaces the buggy Godaddy UI

mvp.item: Variant/SKU management: auto-generate SKUs from variant attributes
mvp.reason: Primary pain point identified in the interview

mvp.item: CSV export: write valid Godaddy-importable CSV
mvp.reason: Delivery mechanism — the only way to push changes to Godaddy

mvp.item: Image handling: organize images into the directory structure Godaddy expects
mvp.reason: Images are part of the product data that Godaddy's importer scans

full.reason: Explicitly requested goal; improves description quality

full.item: Price management: easy bulk or per-product price editing
full.reason: Variants pricing is tedious in Godaddy UI

full.reason: Reduces failed imports and data corruption

full.reason: Real-world organizing principle from the interview
